newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Debt Office warns of bourse fall - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Debt Office warns of bourse fall - paper.

text.p: The head of Sweden's National Debt Office, Thomas Franzen, on Friday warned the Stockholm bourse could face a setback after rallying strongly this year, business daily Dagens Industri reported.
"I am warning that the stock market may get substantially weaker," Franzen said.
"It is naturally always difficult to say how much weaker but there is a risk that people are entering the market without sufficient care."
The Stochkolm bourse has risen nearly 13 percent since the start of the year.
Franzen compared the current bullish mode in Stockholm to the development of the Swedish real estate market in the 1980s when real estate prices soared but then collapsed.
Franzen said his warning was essentially similar to the pessimistic forecast regarding Wall Street voiced by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in early December.
